hxgadget.h File Reference

Detailed Description

This file contains definitions for the Hx UI Toolkit gadget control API. A gadget is a selectable button that can be displayed with an image and/or text. One common use of a gadget is for icons placed in the application bar or in a toolbar.

enum HxGadgetObjectType_t

A gadget can contain one or more objects. The object definition includes a type, which can either by a system type (text or image), or a user type. The toolkit draws a system type using the widget Draw callback, while the application is responsible for drawing objects that are user types.

enum HxGadgetType_t

The gadget type (not to be confused with the gadget object type, below) specifies how the gadget value changes in response to user activity. The gadget value is reflected through a set of images provided in an image button object (see HxImageButtonObj_t).

By default, gadgets are like command buttons: they trigger a message, but do not change value. Toggle gadgets, on the other hand, behave like checkboxes, toggling between the values of 0 and 1.

HxResult HxGadgetDelete ( HxGadget_t *  pGadget  ) 

Delete a gadget control widget.

This function deletes a gadget created from an earlier call to HxGadgetNew.

It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application, since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is deleted. HxGadgetDelete only needs to be called when removing a gadget at runtime.

Parameters:
pGadget IN: Pointer to the gadget to delete
Returns:
HxResult: HxResult

HxResult HxGadgetGetState ( HxGadget_t *  pGadget,
HxGadgetState_t *  pState 
)

Get the visual state of a gadget.

HxGadgetGetState returns the visual state of the gadget, based on whether the gadget is enabled or disabled, the position of the cursor, and the state of the mouse button.

The standard gadget draw routine uses this visual state to select the matching image button variation.

Parameters:
pGadget IN: Pointer to the gadget
pState OUT: Returns the visual state of the gadget
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxGadgetNew ( uint32_t  id,
HxWidget_t *  pParent,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
int32_t  objectCount,
const HxGadgetObject_t *  pObjects,
HxGadgetAttribute_t  attr,
HxGadget_t **  hGadget 
)

Create a gadget control widget.

This function creates a new gadget control widget. The gadget objects are copied into the gadget by the toolkit, so the application is not required to keep its object array.

Text objects are duplicated completely, with local copies of the string and font definition structures stored in the gadget. Image objects have their HxImageDescription_t structures duplicated, but because there is no reference counting implemented in the system, you should NOT call HxImageDescriptionDelete on the description that you've passed into the gadget until you know the gadget has been destroyed.

When using user-defined objects, the application is responsible for initializing both p1 and p2 fields within the HxUserObject_t structure, and it is responsible for freeing any data that those pointers may point to when the gadget is destroyed. One way to do this is to override the destroy callback for the gadget and do your own processing. To destroy any system objects in the gadget, you can save the original destroy callback value and call that to destroy any text and image objects in the list.

The gadget also holds a value setting which is used in conjunction with image button objects to choose a set of images drawn in response to mouse actions or when the the gadget is disabled. User actions do not change the value (except when initialized via HxToggleGadgetNew), but gadget owners can register to receive the gadget selected message and call HxGadgetSetValue in response.

Parameters:
id IN: Unique ID for the widget, defined by app, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
pParent IN: Pointer to "parent" widget containing gadget
pBounds IN: Pointer to bounds of gadget
objectCount IN: Count of objects in this gadget
pObjects IN: Array of objectCount objects
attr IN: Control behavior of the gadget like focusable, and editable
hGadget OUT: Handle to the new gadget; *hGadget is NULL on failure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails, and sets *hGadget to NULL.

Replace an object in a gadget.

This function replaces an object in the object array sent by the application in its call to HxGadgetNew.

The internal structures allocated by the toolkit for the old object is deallocated, and the new objects structures are copied over.

Parameters:
pGadget IN: Pointer to the gadget to delete
index IN: Index of object to replace
pObject IN: Pointer to new object
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if the index is out of bounds.

Create a toggle gadget control widget.

HxToggleGadgetNew creates a gadget control widget in the same fashion as HxGadgetNew, but with the additional logic to toggle between 0 and 1 in response to mouse clicks.

See HxGadgetNew for further details.

Parameters:
id IN: Unique ID for the widget, defined by app, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
pParent IN: Pointer to "parent" widget containing gadget
pBounds IN: Pointer to bounds of gadget
objectCount IN: Count of objects in this gadget
pObjects IN: Array of objectCount objects
attr IN: Control behavior of the gadget like focusable, and editable
hGadget OUT: Handle to the new gadget; *hGadget is NULL on failure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails, and sets *hGadget to NULL.
